_what: The act slides for Seven Days to the Wolves. One card per act of the programme, in the owner's canonical order, each carrying its Roman numeral. `kind: "act"` is the cinematic handoff slide from the website (CinematicTransition.vue), rendered full-frame from its own CSS by cards/render-cards.mjs (cards/act.html).
_order: THE CANONICAL ORDER, codified by the owner on 2026-08-12 and settled: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). Eight acts, each announced by a slide carrying a huge Roman numeral. This list is the show's chapter list: see docs/running-order.md, which is the source of truth, and `tools/megacut.py --chapters`, which derives the timestamped markers from the built programme rather than from a hand-typed table.
_copy: Chapter card copy is REPRODUCED, never authored. Where an act has no authored title, the row is omitted rather than filled -- see `unresolved`. The only strings the owner wrote for this pass are act II's title and the whole of act IV's terminal block, both quoted back verbatim.
_chapters: Every act is to carry chapters, and every `chapters` list below is populated. Five acts -- I, II, III, VI and VII -- carry agent-drafted lists read off the built films, each line cited in its card's `note`; none of those words are the owner's yet, and the rewrite-or-strike decision is recorded in `unresolved`. The merged IV-V slide carries the owner's two authored loglines in the same field, verbatim. A line nobody authored is still omitted, never invented.
_gaps: Act VIII has no film and therefore no card: a slide announcing an act that does not play is worse than a recorded gap. It keeps its numeral in `unresolved` so the numbering cannot drift when it is built. Act II had the same gap until 2026-08-12, when it was built (docs/cuts/02-endless-forms-most-beautiful.md) and this card was added.
_audio: Every card is silent. Putting a bed under one is a licensing decision, the owner's alone.

plates.subtitle: The Kat and the Nat
chapters: With the CNCF Locked in "Oh no what do we do?" mode, two Kubernetes contributors make their own fates.
But not enough volunteers showed up to take notes, leading to some surprises ...
plates.note: ONE slide for two acts, owner instruction: 'give kat/nat one slide since those videos are short'. Their films run 34.0s and 25.3s; two 15s slides announced 59.3s of picture, which is what that note is about. It saves 15s of the programme. Both acts KEEP their numerals and their films -- this merges the announcement, not the acts. ALL OF THE COPY BELOW IS OWNER-AUTHORED, verbatim, and it settled the open question of which title leads: 'retitle this chapter "BIAS FOR ACTION" with the subtitle "The Kat and the Nat"', plus two logline rows. The second was revised twice by the owner and now reads as a continuation of the first -- 'But not enough volunteers showed up to take notes, leading to some surprises ...'. The two earlier wordings both opened 'Backed by community concensus.'; that sentence is no longer on screen. Reproduced as written, including the capital L in 'Locked' and the spelling 'concensus' -- authored copy is reproduced, never silently corrected, and both are flagged in `unresolved` so the owner can decide rather than discover. Act V's authored title, 'Wrong Place, Wrong Time, Right Attitude', is therefore NO LONGER ON SCREEN anywhere -- it is still act V's name in docs/running-order.md, and whether it should survive on the slide is the owner's to say. The terminal block is act IV's five lines, unchanged and still shared, which is why the two slides collapsed cleanly: they differed only in title.
